newsitem.title: USA: USDA panel narrows dairy price formula options.
newsitem.headline: USDA panel narrows dairy price formula options.

text.p: A special committee has identified four possible replacements for the basic formula price that sets the price for milk used in dairy products, the U.S. Agriculture Department said Friday.

USDA initiated the review a year ago as an adjunct to congressional orders to modernize milk marketing orders. They are regional pacts that determine the price of milk bound for grocery stores. The basic formula price is a factor in those so-called fluid milk prices.
In a preliminary report, the committee said it would continue to study alternatives to the basic formula price.
Out of nine options considered by the committee, the four tabbed for further examination were:
--a four-class, multiple component plan to price butterfat, protein and lactose used in cheese (Class III) and butterfat and nonfat solids used in butter and powder (Class IV).

--a three-class, multiple component plan to price protein used in cheese, butterfat used in butter and other nonfat solids used in powder. There would be only one manufacturing class that included cheese, butter and powder.
--a product price formula computed from butter, powder and cheese shares of U.S. production. -
The formula would use seasonal product yields and a California cost-based "make" allowance.

--a competitive pay price series using a national weighted average price paid for Grade A milk used in manufacturing products, updated by a product price formula. The price series would include an adjuster to remove the effect of current regulation and reduce it to a level more comparable to the current basic formula price.
